This year can be said to be the year of super apps. OpenAI recently launched its own super app and openly admitted that the app is "a bit messy." Now the CEO of Microsoft has also confirmed that a dedicated Copilot super app will be launched in the near future.

Microsoft Copilot "super app" will integrate Cowork, chat, coding and other functions into one

Microsoft is developing an AI "super app" that combines Copilot's chat, coding, and intelligent agent functions into one. CEO Satya Nadella said at Wednesday's earnings call that the app will launch this year, covering "consumer and commercial experiences." Nadella said: "Copilot is rapidly evolving from chat functionality to Cowork, and then to Autopilots." He also said: "This quarter we are integrating these Copilot experiences, including coding capabilities, into a single super app... this is a major step, and I look forward to sharing more details later."

OpenAI's process of launching its own "super app" was a complete mess, but this clearly has not deterred other companies from continuing to adopt the super app strategy.

Perhaps Microsoft can more successfully deliver a comprehensive all-in-one app and avoid repeating OpenAI's mistakes.

That said, CEO Nadella has also recently stated that the company is gradually moving away from the traditional app model and focusing on intelligent agents instead. The AI era is still in its nascent stage, and related trends and best practices are constantly evolving.

As for Apple, there are no signs of any shift toward a super app strategy; instead, the company continues to launch various independent and specialized apps. Whether the company will change its strategy in the future remains to be seen.

What are your thoughts on the recent "super app" craze? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
